## AI MAINTENANCE PROTOCOL
- Treat this file as living project memory.
- When changing module boundaries, dependencies, MAF versions, or API contracts, update this file in the same change.
- Verify rules against source files before relying on them.

## OVERVIEW
TinadecCore is a .NET 10 modular monolith built on Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) 1.18.0.
It is the sole state authority for TinadecOffice: sessions, runs, tasks, approvals, events, traces, model routes, tool policy, and workspace-scoped Agent Pack installations. Pack content remains App-owned.
Its normative product boundary and target DmaEA design are in `../docs/tinadec-core-product-definition.zh-CN.md`. MAF is an execution/workflow dependency behind adapters; Tinadec-owned DTOs, configuration, identity, permissions, task lineage, events, snapshots, and evolution records remain the stable product contract.

The current worktree contains 22 source projects and 4 test projects after adding the packable AspNetCore HTTP layer. Solution membership may lag while this change is in progress; count actual `*.csproj`/`*.fsproj` files before updating inventories.

## PUBLIC API VERSION RULE
- TinadecOffice has not released its first formal version. Every public HTTP, OpenAPI, SSE, and WebSocket contract is served under `/api/v1`.
- Do not create `/api/v2` or later prefixes, and do not retain historical compatibility routes, legacy aliases, migration endpoints, or deprecation windows. A breaking change is applied directly to `/api/v1` with its DTOs, events, tests, generated clients, and the Chinese product definition updated in the same change.
- `AgentVersion`, `ModeVersion`, `PromptVersion`, `PolicyVersion`, schema revisions, and content hashes are immutable domain/state bindings; they are not API version numbers.
- The Tool manifest `v2` mentioned in runtime notes is an internal Tool Provider wire/schema format, not an HTTP API prefix; it does not authorize adding `/api/v2`.
- `../docs/tinadec-core-product-definition.zh-CN.md` is the sole normative product document. English material is limited to the fixed terminology glossary; other historical plans are reference only.
- Gateway remains a stateless transport layer. `/api/v1/code/tools/*` and `/api/v1/tool-runtime/*` remain current user-facing direct tool routes for Desktop; these routes are not compatibility shims and must not be removed as legacy cleanup.

Solution folders (`TinadecCore.slnx`):
- `/src/foundation/` — Contracts, Abstractions, Persistence, Strategies

- `/src/host/` — Runtime, AspNetCore, Api

## DEPENDENCY GRAPH
```
Contracts (no deps)
   ↑
Abstractions (Contracts + Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions)
   ↑
Persistence (EF Core + SQLite + Npgsql EF; no business modules)
   ↑
VectorStore (Abstractions + Persistence; no business modules)
   ↑
Tenancy (tenant/workspace identity boundary)
   ↑
Strategies F# (Abstractions)
   ↑
Business modules (Abstractions + Strategies as needed; only DmaEA may reference MAF packages)
   ↑
Runtime (Persistence + all 8 modules + Abstractions)
   ↑
AspNetCore (Runtime + ASP.NET Core FrameworkReference; mountable HTTP surface)
   ↑
Api (AspNetCore, Web SDK)
```

- Business modules do NOT reference each other directly. They collaborate through Abstractions ports.
- Persistence is shared infrastructure, not a harness business module (not counted in the 8-module manifest).
- Only the Api project uses `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`. `AspNetCore` uses plain `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` plus a `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` FrameworkReference so it stays packable; no non-host project may depend on it.
- MAF types are confined to the DmaEA internal adapter and must not appear in other module contracts, HTTP DTOs, persistence, or EventEnvelope.

## PACKAGE DELIVERY
- `Contracts`, `Abstractions`, `Runtime`, and `AspNetCore` are the stable host-facing NuGet package IDs. `AspNetCore` exposes `AddTinadecCoreHttp()` (JSON/problem-details/services), `UseTinadecCoreExceptionHandler()`, and `MapTinadecCore()` (all endpoint groups + health/manifest/readiness diagnostics), so any host can embed the Core HTTP surface without the Api project. Their package readme and current publish commands are documented in `../docs/tinadec-core-packaging.zh-CN.md`; a Core-owned copy lives at `docs/tinadec-core-packaging.zh-CN.md` and the packable csprojs reference it via `..\docs\` (2026-08-29 layout-independence fix), so `dotnet pack` succeeds in both the nested Office layout and the standalone mirror repository.
- Runtime's module and migration project references are packable implementation dependencies so a Runtime nuspec can be restored from one internal feed. They are not additional stable product APIs.
- `Api` remains `IsPackable=false` and is delivered with `dotnet publish` as an executable service directory. Tests remain non-packable.
- MAF 1.18 dependencies may appear in the Runtime implementation dependency graph, but MAF types must remain behind the DmaEA adapter and never enter Contracts, HTTP DTOs, events, or stable SDKs.
- Core packages and Api publish output contain the generic Agent Pack DTO/service/migrations only. `OfficeAgentPack` and other App-owned manifests must not be embedded in Core delivery artifacts.

## PERSISTENCE (DATABASE ABSTRACTION)
- Default provider: **SQLite** local file (`TinadecPersistence:Sqlite:DatabasePath`, default `data/tinadec.db`). No Docker required.
- Optional provider: **PostgreSQL** via `TinadecPersistence:Provider=PostgreSql` + `ConnectionStrings:TinadecCore`.
- Modules register EF Core DbContexts with `options.UseTinadecDatabase(sp)` / `ITinadecDatabaseConfigurer` — business code stays provider-agnostic and uses LINQ.
- `AddTinadecPersistence(configuration, contentRootPath)` registers options, connection info, configurer, Core-owned data paths, migration coordination, and readiness probe. It does not own business entities.
- `MemoryDbContext` owns `projects` and `sessions`; `LifecycleDbContext` owns `runs` and `event_index`. Shared mappings use only provider-neutral CLR types and string-backed state values.
- SQLite uses `Storage.Migrations.Sqlite` and migrates automatically at local startup. PostgreSQL uses `Storage.Migrations.PostgreSql` and migration startup is opt-in through `TinadecPersistence:ApplyMigrationsOnStartup`.
- `.github/workflows/core-storage-postgres.yml` provisions `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` and runs the provider-specific migration/storage contract test.
- Session histories atomically replace files under `data/sessions/`; task snapshots, immutable JSONL events, and artifacts live under `data/tasks/`, `data/events/`, and `data/artifacts/`.
- `GET /api/v1/readiness` includes `storage: { provider, state, detail }` from `IDatabaseReadiness` (`SELECT 1` probe).
- `ITenantContextAccessor` is the sole request isolation port. Development uses the configured bootstrap identity; production must replace it with a verified external identity adapter.
- `IContentStore` uses tenant/workspace-partitioned immutable references. `ISecretStore` exposes secret references only; database rows must not carry secret values.
- `IProjectVectorDatabase` is Persistence's provider-specific vector storage port. SQLite stores one `sqlite-vec` database per tenant/workspace/project under `data/vectors/`; PostgreSQL uses `pgvector` via `PostgresProjectVectorDatabase` (Npgsql + `Vector` type, shared `vector_chunks`/`vector_collections` tables, `vector_cosine_ops` ivfflat/hnsw, `Migration 202608260001_VectorStorePgVector`).
- `VectorStore` is a foundation capability, not a business module. It owns chunking, embedding requests, and semantic retrieval through `IVectorStore`; callers do not pass embeddings or database details.
- Models, prompts, agents, integrations, policy/approval, run configuration bindings, artifacts, and control-event indexes now have module-owned provider-neutral DbContexts. Their current projections reference immutable versions or ContentStore bodies.
- `AgentConfigurationDbContext` also owns seven workspace-scoped Pack tables: installations, immutable versions, managed resources, per-version bindings, 15-minute previews, default adoptions, and idempotency operation receipts. Migration `202608250001_AgentPacks` exists for SQLite and PostgreSQL.

## MAF VERSIONS (locked in Directory.Packages.props)
- `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Abstractions` 1.18.0
- `Microsoft.Agents.AI` 1.18.0
- `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows` 1.18.0
- `Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI` 1.18.0
- MAF-specific behavior stays behind `DmaEA/Maf18RuntimeAdapter.cs`: Core owns durable permission, approval, checkpoint, tool receipt, and recovery state.
- Compaction preserves atomic function-call/result groups; usage is normalized to the provider-neutral `ModelUsage`; OpenTelemetry keeps sensitive data disabled.
- MAF automatic-approval iteration limits are only a ceiling for Core tool-round budgets. They never grant authority or bypass the durable Tool Dispatcher.

## ASP.NET CORE SECURITY BASELINE
- `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` are pinned to `10.0.11`.
- `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`, `.Abstractions`, and `Options.ConfigurationExtensions` are pinned to the required `10.0.11` patch level.
- `Microsoft.OpenApi` resolves transitively to `2.7.5`, removing the `2.0.0` exposure tracked as `GHSA-v5pm-xwqc-g5wc`.
- Verify with `dotnet list TinadecCore/TinadecCore.slnx package --vulnerable --include-transitive` after package changes.

## MODULE REGISTRATION
- Each module implements `IModuleRegistrar` with an explicit `Register(ITinadecCoreBuilder)` method.
- `Runtime/TinadecCoreServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` provides:
  - `AddTinadecCore()` — registers all 8 modules (full composition).
  - `AddTinadecCoreMinimal()` — registers only DmaEA, Models, Lifecycle (trimming proof).
- No reflection scanning. Each `AddTinadec...()` extension is explicit.
- `VectorStoreModuleRegistrar` is registered before business modules. `Models` implements `IEmbeddingProvider`; until a real embedding route/provider exists, indexing returns an explicit unavailable result.
- `DmaEAModuleRegistrar` registers `AgentRuntimeConfigurationStore` and its `IAgentRuntimeConfiguration` port. The singleton remains lazy until a consumer resolves it; the full-duplex engine resolves and freezes a profile per run.

## API ENDPOINTS (port 48731)

### Core endpoints (fully implemented)
| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/v1/health` | GET | `{name, status, version, time}` health structure. |
| `/api/v1/harness/manifest` | GET | Returns dual-layer Agent, MAF version, 8 module descriptors, framework info. |
| `/api/v1/readiness` | GET | MAF assemblies loadable = ready; unconfigured modules use `warning` + `not_configured`. |
| `/api/v1/projects` | GET/POST | Lists and creates projects with a canonical unique root path. |
| `/api/v1/sessions` | GET/POST | Lists and creates session metadata. |
| `/api/v1/sessions/{id}` | PATCH | Updates the session title. |
| `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages` | GET/POST | Reads/writes versioned Core-owned history files. |
| `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/runs` | GET | Lists durable lifecycle run metadata. |
| `/api/v1/events` | GET SSE | Replays indexed JSONL events, then follows durable additions with SSE heartbeat; optionally filters by session and sequence. The initial replay honors `after_seq`/`Last-Event-ID`; follow cycles poll a timestamp watermark (`StorageLifecycleService.FollowEventsAsync`, 2s overlap) and de-duplicate by per-run sequence, so no follow cycle rescans the whole journal. |
| `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/invoke-stream` | POST SSE | Full-duplex DmaEA invocation (see `DmaeaEndpoints.cs` + `FullDuplexRunEngine`): idempotent admission, `context_revision` checks/patches, governance coordination → task planning → execution → supervision → meeting finalization, spawn/lineage, durable ack/delta/done/error SSE with replay/follow, run control, active-run limits, and restart recovery. |
| `/api/v1/runs/{runId}/orchestration` | GET | Replay-derived run/task/step/agent-instance/supervision projection. |
| `/api/v1/runs/{runId}/context-versions` | GET | Context revision/patch history for a run. |
| `/api/v1/runs/{runId}/stream` | GET SSE | Durable stream replay/follow by turn. |
| `/api/v1/runs/{runId}/control` | POST | cancel/pause/resume run control. |
| `/api/v1/agent-evolution/proposals` | GET | Agent candidate proposals (status-filterable). |
| `/api/v1/agent-evolution/generate` | POST | Persists a run-scoped agent candidate proposal (source instance must be a generated worker or `experience_curator`). |
| `/api/v1/agent-evolution/proposals/{candidateId}/promote` / `reject` | POST | Decides a proposed candidate; promotion creates an immutable promoted agent profile version. |
| `/api/v1/agent-packs` / `/api/v1/agent-packs/{packId}` | GET | Lists or reads workspace-scoped installations and exact resource bindings; detail returns an ETag revision. |
| `/api/v1/agent-packs/install-preview` | POST | Owner-only validation/preview of an RFC 8785/JCS SHA-256 envelope; preview expires after 15 minutes. |
| `/api/v1/agent-packs/{packId}` | PUT | Applies the same previewed envelope with `Idempotency-Key`; upgrades require `If-Match`. |
| `/api/v1/model-resolution/preview` | POST | What-if resolution of the effective model strategy chain (agent + mode-node override + session override) without persisting. |
| `/api/v1/model-references` | GET | Back-references (agents, modes, routes, recent invocations) for a provider instance + model pair. |
| `/api/v1/model-invocations` | GET | Cursor-paged durable invocation attribution log; filters by run/agent/mode/provider/model/status/time window. |

### Gateway proxy endpoints
`AspNetCore/Endpoints/ControlPlaneEndpoints.cs` owns durable model provider/route, prompt fragment, agent, and approval projections; `/api/v1/approvals` has no client-side creation POST. `UserToolActionEndpoints.cs` owns user tool action create/detail/resume/snapshot-override/recovery-decision, while `GovernanceEndpoints.cs` owns permission/grant/delegation/lease routes and wakes user actions after decisions. Recovery decisions only mark an unknown user action completed or failed; they never replay the provider. These handlers use the tenant accessor, module DbContexts, immutable ContentStore versions, SecretStore references, and `If-Match` revision checks. Workspace defaults (with ETag/If-Match) are mapped by `AgentConfigurationEndpoints.cs`; filesystem/Git snapshots by `WorkspaceSnapshotEndpoints.cs`. Remaining Gateway-proxied runtime, extension, MCP, and debug endpoints stay in `StubEndpoints.cs`. Unavailable mutations return structured 501 responses rather than pretending to execute.

Stub groups:
- **Readiness**: `doctor`, `model-readiness`, `model-catalog-readiness`, `tool-layer-readiness`
- **Projects/Sessions**: `context-packs`, `supervision-findings` (empty `[]` until persisted); `invoke-stream`, `orchestration`, `tool-executions`, and `task-nodes` are implemented in `AspNetCore/Endpoints/DmaeaEndpoints.cs`; full-duplex controls, context versions, and run-scoped projections are covered by the same endpoints.
- **Tools**: `tools`, `tools/search`, `tools/shell`, `runs/{runId}/tools/{toolId}/execute`
- **Approvals**: `approvals` (GET/detail), `approvals/{id}/decision`; client creation is forbidden. Use `user/tool-actions` for user work and Tool Dispatcher for agent work.
- **Model**: `model-provider-templates`, `model-providers` (CRUD + canonical model refresh), `model-routes`, `model-settings` (GET/PUT) — versioned proxy/client composition
- **Prompts**: `prompt-fragments` (CRUD), `prompt-context/preview`, versions, effectiveness, signals, compare
- **Agents**: `agents`, `agent-modes`, prompt pipelines and `workspace-defaults` use versioned control-plane handlers; `agent-packs` uses `AgentPackEndpoints`/`AgentPackService`; `agent-candidates` is review-driven (`MemoryReviewEndpoints.cs`) and `agent-evolution/*` is implemented in `AspNetCore/Endpoints/EvolutionEndpoints.cs`
- **Market/Extensions**: `market/sources`, `market/catalog`, `extensions/*`
- **MCP/ACP**: `mcp/servers`, `acp/adapters`
- **Debug**: `debug/traces`, `debug/spans`, `debug/metrics`, `debug/snapshot`, `debug/diagnostics`, `debug/processes`, `debug/simulate/*`, `debug/breakpoints`

`GET /api/v1/debug/snapshot/{sessionId}` is a durable, tenant/workspace-scoped
`session_runtime` projection from Lifecycle. Its explicit
`source=lifecycle_projection` payload contains run/task/event metadata only;
filesystem workspace snapshots, conversation context snapshots, and MAF run
checkpoints remain separate resources.

All JSON output uses `snake_case` via `JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower`.

## F# INTEROP RULES
- F# modules compile to static classes in C#.
- Use `using TinadecCore.Strategies;` then `LoopDetection.detectRepeatCalls(...)`.
- F# public functions return only C#-compatible types: `int[]`, `bool`, `double`, `(string, float)[]`.
- No F# DU, list, option, async, or curried function in public signatures.

## CONVENTIONS
- `snake_case` JSON at the API boundary; C# properties use PascalCase.
- Console log discipline: `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` is pinned to `Warning` in `Api/appsettings.json` (Information-level EF command logs once flooded startup with ~1900 repetitive SQL lines; measured before/after 2026-08-23). Startup phases stay one-line quiet: `StorageMigrationRunner` logs a single context-count summary and `DevSeed` logs only when it actually seeds. To inspect SQL temporarily, override via environment (`Logging__LogLevel__Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore=Information`) or user-secrets — do not commit the filter change.
- `EventEnvelope` uses schema version 1.0 and snake_case. No MAF/F# types in payload.
- `ModuleDescriptor.RegistrationStatus`: `Registered`, `NotConfigured`, `Disabled`.
- Gateway transparently proxies all Core endpoints; no Gateway changes needed for stub endpoints.
- Canonical layers are the governance layer (`operation`) and execution layer (`execution`). `planning` is not a public layer name; new Core APIs, events, persisted configuration versions, and Desktop-visible values must write `operation`.
- `Configuration/default-agent-runtime.toml` is a read-only, annotated baseline copied to DmaEA output. `AgentRuntimeConfigurationStore` validates its meeting-only user-output rule, mode/profile bindings, aliases, and budgets when resolved; valid edits replace that store's in-memory snapshot and invalid edits retain its last valid snapshot. The full-duplex engine freezes a profile per run; workspace overrides and readiness exposure remain open.
- Pack-managed Agent/Mode/Prompt resources return RFC9457 `managed_resource_read_only` from normal draft/publish/archive writes. Clone/create produces user-owned resources; never add an Office-specific exception to Core.

## CURRENT STATE (durable control plane + full-duplex DmaEA runtime)
- The current Core tree contains 22 source projects (including the packable AspNetCore HTTP layer) and 4 test projects, including Governance and its contract tests.
- Shared storage is registered with four relational index tables and Core-owned file stores. Startup reconciles indexed events from valid JSONL records and reports an incomplete final JSONL line as a storage diagnostic.
- Model/provider/route, prompt fragment, agent, and approval projections are persisted with tenant/workspace isolation and immutable ContentStore versions. Provider credentials use the platform SecretStore and never appear in responses.
- **DmaEA invocation runtime is implemented (2026-08-05)**: `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/invoke-stream` appends the user message (Desktop does not double-write), then runs the current planning (`PlanningAgent`) and execution (`ExecutionAgent`) agents over the `chat` model route resolved via `IChatResolver` (OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `ChatClientAgent` per task). The endpoint streams one terminal SSE chunk (`kind:done` on success, `kind:error` + `error_category:runtime` otherwise); it is request-bound, does not persist an assistant message, and does not provide delta/ack/usage chunks. The orchestrator persists `run.started`/`task_graph.created`/`task.assigned`/`step.result.created`/`run.failed` events plus task snapshots via `ILifecycleManager` (`UpdateTaskSnapshotAsync` bumps `TaskRevision`). `GET .../orchestration`, `.../tool-executions`, and `.../task-nodes` project from replayed events. `DevSeed` (in `Runtime/DevSeed.cs`, invoked from Api `Program.cs`) idempotently seeds a `chat` route + OpenAI provider (no API key stored) + `planner`/`executor` agents; without a stored key runs fail cleanly (`run.failed`, error chunk — never fake success). Failed runs keep `running` status for audit; only success completes.
- **Full-duplex runtime is implemented and tested**: `FullDuplexRunEngine` + `FullDuplexRunCoordinator` drive `invoke-stream` with idempotent client-message-id admission, `context_revision` snapshots and meeting context patches (supplement/goal_adjustment/status_query), governance coordination → task planning → execution → supervision → meeting finalization, worker spawn/lineage via `AgentInstanceService` (budgets from the frozen runtime profile), durable SSE (ack/delta/done/error) with replay/follow, run control (cancel/pause/resume), active-run limits, and restart recovery through leased checkpoints (`RunRecoveryHostedService`). `agent_instances`/`agent_candidates` projections and candidate review (`MemoryReviewEndpoints`) back the agent-evolution surface (`EvolutionEndpoints.cs`: generate/promote/reject, no longer 501). Tests use scripted chat clients (`FullDuplexEndpointTests`), temp-DB factories, and an empty v2 tool-manifest resolver.
- **Tool chain wired end-to-end (2026-08-18, tests green)**: `TinadecToolsProcessManager` auto-probes `TinadecTools:ExecutablePath` (content root, then `TinadecTools/bin/{Debug|Release}/net10.0/`) when null, hosts one v2-manifest child process per workspace root on a BOM-free UTF-8 line-delimited JSON pipe (`new UTF8Encoding(false)` — `Encoding.UTF8` emits an EF-BB-BF preamble that corrupts the first JSON byte on the wire). `ToolManifestSnapshotResolver` freezes the authorized manifest per run; `ToolInvocationScopeResolver` verifies the frozen hash at resume; `ToolDispatcher` persists an execution before invoking the deterministic PDP, idempotently creates permission requests/leases, pauses in `awaiting_delegate`/`awaiting_user`, and only then creates a one-time ActionApproval for required writes. `ToolApprovalCoordinator` and `GovernanceService` enforce execution/run/task/agent/tool/parameter bindings, lease TTL/use limits, explicit deny and nonce consumption; decisions wake the run via `engine.EnqueueAsync(runId)`. `ToolChainEndpointTests` runs one full-duplex run→pending-approval→approve→resume→real `write_file` E2E through HTTP (approval stream stays open while pending; resume completes the same stream; `probe.txt` is really written); `TinadecToolsProcessTests` covers the real child process (5 tests). The TinadecTools project reference in Api.Tests is conditional (`Exists()` on the sibling monorepo path), and the four real-process entry points (`TinadecToolsProcessTests` plus the three `[RequiresTinadecToolsFact]` write-path tests) skip cleanly when the apphost binary is absent, so a Core-only showcase mirror builds and tests green without TinadecTools (`scripts/showcase/sync-showcase.ps1` excludes the process-test file from the mirror). `GET /api/v1/tool-layer-readiness` reports the real manifest and frozen-profile execution-agent scopes, degrading to warning notes when no default workspace root is configured. The generic `IToolProvider` contract is host-decoupled and verified by an in-process fake-provider E2E (`WorkerWriteFile_ThroughInProcessFakeProvider_DispatchLoopCompletesWithoutTinadecTools`): with `IToolProvider` replaced in DI, the full approval→resume→dispatch loop completes and Core never spawns the TinadecTools binary.
- **Multi-protocol chat support (2026-08-19, tests green)**: `ChatResolution` carries a `Protocol` value (`ChatProtocols`: `openai-chat` default, `openai-responses`, `anthropic-messages`). `ModelProvider.ResolveChatAsync` reads the provider config JSON `protocol` key and falls back to driver inference (`anthropic`/`claude` → anthropic-messages, `openai-responses` → openai-responses). `AgentChatClientFactory` (DmaEA, replaces `OpenAiAgentChatClientFactory`) branches on the protocol: OpenAI SDK chat completions, `GetResponsesClient().AsIChatClient(model)` (OPENAI001 experimental surface deliberately suppressed), or `Anthropic.SDK` 5.10.0 whose `MessagesEndpoint` implements `IChatClient` directly (base URL normalized to the SDK's `{version}/{endpoint}` format — a stored trailing `/v1` is stripped). `GET /api/v1/model-provider-templates` returns three protocol templates; `ToProvider` exposes `protocol`; `RefreshProviderModels` uses `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` headers for anthropic-messages discovery. No DB schema change — `protocol` lives in the immutable provider config JSON blob.
- **Operation/execution configuration foundation exists (2026-08-17)**: `Configuration/default-agent-runtime.toml` defines `conversation`/`space` modes, the `space.full_duplex` profile, `im`/`hub` aliases, meeting-only `direct_user_output`, candidate-only memory policy, and default spawn/scheduling budgets. `AgentRuntimeConfigurationStore` can parse, validate, hash, and valid-only hot-reload snapshots when resolved. `AgentControlDbContext` now contains `agent_instances`, `agent_candidates`, and `runtime_profile_overrides` projections. The full-duplex engine resolves and freezes the profile per run; the baseline orchestrator's legacy planning-layer selection and workspace overrides plus readiness diagnostic exposure were superseded by the 2026-08-27 agent-directory refactor below.
- **CLI runtime connect closed loop (2026-08-21, Api tests 68/68 green)**: `GET /api/v1/model-providers/cli/discover` (`ControlPlaneService.DiscoverCliRuntimes`) probes installed CLI binaries with `--version` reachability and reports `missing`/`found`/`configured` candidates — `binary_path` is emitted only after the version probe succeeds. `POST /api/v1/model-providers/cli/connect` (`ConnectCliRuntime`) validates `driver`/`binary_path`, infers the protocol via `ChatProtocols.InferFromDriver` (`acp` for `claude-cli`/`codex-cli`/`cursor-acp`, `opencode-serve` for `opencode`), and calls `CliProcessManager.EnsureRunningAsync` to spawn or reuse the CLI service (ACP `--acp-port` free-port launch or `opencode serve --port`; `ResponseHeadersRead` reachability probe; `FirstValueAsync` returns null fast when the process exits; `Win32Exception` wraps to `CLI_CONNECT_FAILED` 502), then persists an enabled provider carrying the reachable `server_url` + effective launch args — routes are never touched. `CliRuntime` adds the ACP drivers (JSON-RPC 2.0 over SSE `AcpChatClient`) and `opencode serve` (`OpenCodeChatClient`); both are Microsoft.Extensions.AI `IChatClient`s usable as full-duplex run backends.
- **智能体配置与全双工重构收口 (2026-08-22)**: `AgentConfiguration`、session `mode_version_id`、`InteractionsEndpoints`、Prompt 图校验、工具交集和逐 Agent 模型策略已接入全双工冻结配置。关系库发布 ModeVersion 是正式 roster 事实源；无绑定时才回落 TOML，TOML 继续提供通用策略预算。
- **Generic Agent Pack + Office runtime closure (2026-08-25)**: `IAgentPackService`/`AgentPackService` and four `/api/v1/agent-packs*` endpoints validate SemVer, internal references, dual-layer topology, capabilities, RFC 8785/JCS digest and owner scope, then install Prompt -> Agent -> Mode -> eligible defaults atomically. Same version/hash is no-op, hash/resource/revision conflicts fail closed, lower bundled versions return `newer_installed`, equivalent legacy resources may be adopted, and custom defaults are preserved. `DevSeed` no longer writes Office Agent/Prompt/Mode/defaults; it retains only generic chat-route + planner/executor bootstrap. Mode snapshots pin exact AgentVersion/PromptVersion IDs and hashes; frozen prompts are assembled for meeting/planner/supervisor/worker, specialist selection is deterministic and fail-closed, assignment is persisted before invocation, and only meeting answers the user. The four dormant operation roles remain frozen without instances/events.
- **Composer modes wired to pack topologies (2026-08-26, Api tests 116 green)**: the bundled Office pack is `0.2.0` with **7 modes** — `default-mode` (space.full_duplex full roster) plus `conversation.plan/spec/ask/vibe/auto/agent` whose node subsets mirror the TOML profiles' `operation_agents` and each carry that mode's legitimate worker subset (worker selection only sees the frozen roster of the active mode and fails closed without coverage). `POST /sessions/{id}/interactions` accepts `agent_mode` (plan|spec|ask|vibe|auto|agent): resolution order is explicit `mode_version_id` > latest published `conversation.{agent_mode}` version for the workspace > the session's existing mode; the resolved version persists via `UpdateSessionModeAsync` and admission runs under the `conversation` application semantics (`space`+`agent` stays the no-selection default). Unknown values return 400 `invalid_request`. `GET /api/v1/agent-modes/{id}` now returns the current topology for any live status — draft projection for drafts, published projection (+ `managed: true`) for published/pack-managed modes — so the Desktop canvas can render installed modes; the draft-only guard remains on update/publish writes. Gateway `sessionMapper` forwards `mode_version_id`/`meeting_model_override` (structured `{provider_instance_id, model}`; the legacy free-text `meeting_model` and split provider column were removed by the 2026-08-27 refactor), and `interactionsMapper` validates the `agent_mode` enum before passthrough.
- Gateway-proxied endpoints outside the durable control-plane, DmaEA, and agent-evolution surface remain stubs: GET returns empty/default responses and unsupported writes return structured `501 capability_unavailable`.
- The deleted `model-center/overview`, `agent-center/overview`, and flat agent runtime-binding routes are not compatibility surfaces. Clients compose centers from versioned Core APIs through Gateway.
- **Workspace snapshot/defaults surfaces (2026-08-22)**: `IWorkspaceSnapshotProvider` has filesystem and safe-argument-list Git implementations; `IWorkspaceSnapshotService` persists provider-neutral snapshots plus a separate `session_metadata_snapshots` projection. Git captures HEAD/ref, index/tree, worktree, binary patches, untracked/deleted/conflict paths; restore validates current state and is idempotent. `UserToolActionService` and `ToolDispatcher` capture high-risk write snapshots before permission/action approval; snapshot failure blocks until a current-user one-time override records a non-reversible audit mark. `WorkspaceDefaults` has tenant/workspace-scoped draft/publish/archive handlers with ETag/If-Match checks. SQLite and PostgreSQL both receive the schema and content is stored through the immutable ContentStore.
- **User tool governance (2026-08-22)**: `UserToolAction` is a durable action outside the run/task/agent graph. Core derives the principal from tenant context and freezes parameters, Tool Provider protocol/manifest identity, the complete v2 descriptor (schema/risk/mutation/approval/retry semantics), and snapshot bindings. Every resume verifies the live manifest, descriptor, confirmation fields, and parameters before consuming authorization or calling the provider. A serialized startup recovery pass idempotently advances decided waiting actions, uses an action-status CAS to prevent concurrent provider calls, and converts restart-orphaned `running` actions to `outcome_unknown` without replay. It currently scans only `ITenantContextAccessor.Current`, which is sufficient for the local single-workspace host; cloud multi-tenant recovery still requires a tenant scheduler and distributed claim. The action shares PDP/lease/ActionApproval with agent execution, stores nonce hashes plus protected material references, and never emits nonce material in DTOs or Gateway responses; invalid approval binding, schema/manifest drift, lease expiry/revocation, and unknown external outcomes fail closed. Snapshot override and remote push persist `non_reversible` plus public compensation guidance.
- **模型与智能体控制面重构 (2026-08-27)**: per-agent model strategy is `inherit|route|fixed` only — `model_routes` carry ordered `model_route_candidates` (`position`, migration `202608270002_ModelRoutesV2`); `fixed` binds `provider_instance_id` + optional `model` (null allowed for CLI/ACP provider instances); the legacy parent-select/cli/acp strategy kinds and the profile write path are gone (migration `202608270004` drops those tables). `IAgentModelResolver` (`Runtime/AgentModelResolver.cs`) is the single resolution + attribution authority: every chat invocation persists a `model_invocations` row (call_id/attempt, `strategy_source`, route + provider version ids, model/protocol, `fallback_position`, status, token usage) indexed per run/agent/mode/provider (`202608270003_ModelInvocations`). Sessions store a structured `meeting_model_override` (`provider_instance_id` + `model`, `202608270005_StructuredMeetingModelOverride`), replacing the old free-text model + split provider columns. Agent definitions carry `source_kind` (`bootstrap|pack|custom|missing_reference`), `source_key`, and `managed` (unique per workspace, `202608270001_AgentModelDirectory`); `mode_nodes` gained `model_strategy_override`; `Runtime/BootstrapAgentDirectory.cs` seeds the bootstrap directory. New endpoints in `ModelAgentControlEndpoints.cs`: `POST /api/v1/model-resolution/preview` (what-if chain without persisting), `GET /api/v1/model-references` (agent/mode/route/recent-invocation back-references for a provider + model), `GET /api/v1/model-invocations` (cursor-paged attribution log); `GET /api/v1/agents` in `AgentConfigurationEndpoints.cs` returns the full directory projection (source identity, mode usages, effective strategy preview, recent invocation). The legacy catalog route and the standalone `application-modes` projection were deleted — no compatibility aliases. SQLite keeps every `DateTimeOffset` ordering client-side after materialization.
- Desktop frontend can load without connection errors when Gateway proxies to Core.
- No real provider calls (API key must be configured via SecretStore) and no configured embedding route.
- `loop_guard`, `lifecycle`, and `dma_ea` are `Registered`; other modules are `NotConfigured`.
- The prior `Microsoft.OpenApi` 2.0.0 high-severity advisory is resolved by the ASP.NET Core 10.0.11 package baseline; the transitive package now resolves to 2.7.5.

- Prompt version analytics/rollback and model-driven agent proposal generation inside runs (an `experience_curator` evolution agent)
- Additional business schemas beyond the storage foundation, model/provider configuration, prompt/agent configuration, and approval configuration
- Vector store selection
- Scheduling (invocation runtime and tool dispatch are implemented; the scheduling write paths remain 501)
- Workspace runtime-profile overrides and configuration diagnostics surfaced through readiness (the readiness diagnostic remains open)
- Candidate-only long-term memory review, promotion/revocation, retrieval injection, and isolated memory-audit state
- Real business logic behind the remaining stub endpoints (currently return empty/501)
